topics: The OpenGL ES Shading Language (GLSL ES)

chunks.text: With the advent of HTML5, browsers evolved from simple presentation engines to sophisticated application platforms, creating a need for 3D graphics capabilities. Traditionally, compelling 3D graphics required stand-alone applications using C or C++ with libraries like OpenGL and Direct3D. WebGL was designed to fill the role of creating the visual layer for browser-based 3D applications and experiences.

WebGL advantages include: (1) It is supported as the browser's default built-in technology for rendering 3D graphics — no special plug-ins or libraries required. (2) It is cross-platform. (3) It uses familiar HTML and JavaScript with extra code for 3D graphics. (4) It enables rich user interfaces, 3D games, and visualization of internet data. (5) Development requires only a text editor and browser. (6) Applications can be published using standard web technologies. (7) It leverages full browser functionality. WebGL is described as 'OpenGL for web browsers.'

chunks.topic: The OpenGL ES Shading Language (GLSL ES)
chunks.text: The programming language used to create shaders is called a shading language. OpenGL ES 2.0 uses the OpenGL ES Shading Language (GLSL ES), which is based on GLSL. Because WebGL is based on OpenGL ES 2.0, it also uses GLSL ES for creating shaders. Web pages using WebGL are therefore created using three languages: HTML5 (as a Hypertext Markup Language), JavaScript, and GLSL ES.
